items.title: Terri Lyne Carrington interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003
items.q: innately it was the same way I approached music even before I played with him

ctx.x: You said Herbie Hancock, going back to him for a moment, spoils you for playing with other people? Is that right?

Oh God, yeah. I mean he’s my favorite pianist. And he’s just so open and so receptive musically. He just reacts. He’s the kind of musician that I try to be as well so I really connect with his way because innately it was the same way I approached music even before I played with him. You know you’re really reacting to what you’re hearing. And you know you have the things that you can do but you don’t really just resort to the licks, resort to oh I know I can play this so let me play this, as well as like…
Do you think the proliferation of jazz schools has affected that thing you mentioned about being able to recognize people from their sound?
